harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now serves HTTPS on 10.100.219.10:8443 using a 30-day self-signed certificate. A persistent daily systemd timer renews certificates within seven days of expiry, and the running service reloads them without dropping requests. Configuration and certificate persisted across the mandatory node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled the rotating-https systemd service.
Installed and enabled the rotating-https-renew persistent timer.
Configured certificates with DNS:node1 and IP:10.100.219.10 SANs.
Verified 150 continuous requests during rotation with zero failures and an unchanged server PID.
Verified expiry-triggered renewal through the systemd renewal unit.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified service, timer, certificate, and HTTPS response recovery.

evidence.summary: Direct listener, TLS handshake, certificate SAN, and successful HTTPS response were observed before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before expiry
evidence.summary: The persistent renewal timer is enabled. A one-day certificate inside the seven-day renewal window was automatically replaced through the systemd renewal unit with a certificate valid for 30 days.

evidence.requirement: Pick up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: The served certificate serial changed while the process PID stayed constant; all 150 concurrent test requests succeeded without failures.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 8d1d94e2-39c3-492e-b9eb-974d111d2137; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID was f7ae554f-ddbb-4eef-b149-f516e804bc41; afterward the system was running, HTTPS and the timer were active/enabled, the response succeeded, and the served certificate matched the persisted certificate.
